data.long_meaning: In Greek mythology, Meryl means 'Sea of Bitter'. This name was given to a nymph who protected sailors from the treacherous waters of the sea. The name Meryl carries the meaning “Sea of bitter” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Meryl usually hope their child will grow to embody sea of bitter and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Meryl belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Sea of bitter.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Meryl total 1, giving a life-path number of 1. Number 1 is linked with Sun and with the qualities of leadership, independence and initiative.

in_hebrew.name: מריל
in_hebrew.long_meaning: From the Hebrew word 'marah' meaning 'bitter', this name could be derived from the Hebrew root 'ral' meaning 'to rest'. Thus, 'Meryl' could mean 'restful' or 'tranquil'.

in_greek.name: Μερυλλή
in_greek.long_meaning: In Greek mythology, 'Meryl' could be derived from 'Meryllos', the name of a sea god, and 'Mercy', the name of the goddess of mercy. Thus, 'Meryl' could mean 'sea of the goddess Mercy'.

in_latin.name: Meryllia
in_latin.long_meaning: From the Latin word 'merus' meaning 'pure' or 'innocent', and the suffix '-illa' meaning 'little' or 'small', 'Meryl' could mean 'merry' or 'joyful'.

in_english.name: Meryl
in_english.long_meaning: From the Welsh name 'Mair', meaning 'rebellious' or 'bitter', 'Meryl' could be derived from this root.

data.cultural_impact: Meryl is a unique and beautiful name in the English-speaking world, mainly due to its association with actress Meryl Streep. She has made an indelible mark in the film industry and has won numerous awards for her outstanding performances. This name now stands for resilience, adaptability, and artistic excellence.
data.spiritual_significance: In its original Greek mythological context, Meryl represents the power and protection that one can find in the depths of the sea, even in the face of difficult and bitter experiences. It serves as a reminder that just as the sea provides sustenance and life, God is with us in our most trying times and offers us His grace and love. The name Meryl, therefore, embodies the spiritual qualities of strength, perseverance, and the hope of a brighter future.
